requirements.text: Initialize a new high-priority case on this
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND account_id = 29 AND contact_id = 61 AND product_id = 55 AND channel = 'email' AND priority = 'high' AND state = 'new'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest case_id on the seed is 1232)
Stephanie Clark is user 322, whose only contact is 61 on account 29
Docker Enterprise Variant 35 is product 55; the account holds an active entitlement for it (272) and an in-use installed product (155)
channel email from 'received through an email'
state new is the policy's default for a new case
installed_product_id is not tested: the request names the product only

requirements.text: Emily Moore should be assigned to Stephanie Clark's new case
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND assigned_to = 701
requirements.source: Validating user and group assignment to the case.
assumptions: Emily Moore is user 701, an active agent, the only user of that name
the case was meant for Mario Perry (532), but the request names Emily Moore instead

requirements.text: Make sure the Field Service Coordination_2 group takes this under their wing
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND assignment_group_id = 34
requirements.source: Validating user and group assignment to the case.
assumptions: Field Service Coordination_2 is group 34 (active); the similarly named groups 14, 54 and 74 are other rows

requirements.text: Emily Moore should be assigned to Stephanie Clark's new case
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 960 AND group_id = 34 AND user_id = 701
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the policy requires the assigned user to be a member of the assignment group
Emily Moore belongs only to group 24 on the seed, so a membership in group 34 must be added
the acting user is an admin, whom the policy allows to create group memberships
id assumed next in sequence (highest member_id on the seed is 959)

requirements.text: he left the company yesterday, so he is not active anymore
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id = 532 AND active = 0
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the request says Mario Perry (user 532) is no longer active, while the seed still has him active
the acting user is an admin, whom the policy allows to deactivate users

requirements.text: This case was supposed to be assigned to Mario Perry, but he left the company yesterday
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE contact_id = 61 AND assigned_to = 532
assumptions: the request rules out Mario Perry as assignee and the policy requires an active assignee, so no case of Stephanie Clark's may be assigned to him

requirements.text: please provide report to Stephanie with related article
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 734 AND case_id = 1233 AND knowledge_id = 81 AND email = 'stephanie.clark4@jonesgoodmanandreynolds.com' AND type = 'report' AND status = 'success'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest notification_id on the seed is 733)
the report concerns the new case, so case_id is the new case 1233
the related article is knowledge 81, the only article for product 55; it is published and external, so the customer may view it
type report from 'provide report'
status success kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

notes:
The case's short_description follows a policy template ('Product: ' + product name + ', Issue: ...') that no benchmark check tests, so it is left out.
The request asks for a report carrying the related article, not for the article to be linked to the case, and the case is not asked to be investigated, so no case_knowledge link is required. No interaction record is asked for and no listed tool writes the interaction table.
Mario Perry still holds open case 369 for another contact and belongs to groups 42, 68 and 72; the request does not ask for either to change, so neither is tested.
The benchmark checks select the case by the contact's name and the membership by names; here they are anchored on the next ids, which is stricter.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that no case of Stephanie Clark's (contact 61) is assigned to Mario Perry (532): one pass wrote it, the other did not; kept because the request rules him out as assignee and the policy requires an assignee to be active, as with any other forbidden assignment.
